questions.question:
Identify the Buddhist architectural structure based on the given characteristics:
1. Served as meditation cells and living quarters for monks.
2. Commonly used by wandering monks during the rainy season.
3. Famous examples are found at Ajanta, Ellora, Nasik, Karle, Kanheri, and Bagh.
questions.solution:
Viharas
These were monasteries consisting of small cells arranged around a courtyard. They served as dwelling places and meditation halls for Buddhist monks, especially during the rainy season. Some of the finest rock-cut viharas are located at Ajanta and Ellora (Maharashtra), Nasik, Karle, Kanheri, and Bagh.

questions.question: Buddha meditated for days on end under a peepal tree at ______ where he attained enlightenment.
questions.solution:
Bodh Gaya
Gautam Buddha (Siddhartha, Sakyamuni & Tathagata):
  • Father: Suddhodana
  • Mother: Mayadevi
  • Birth Place (563 B.C.): Lumbini (Nepal), Capital of Sakya republic
  • Teachers: Alarakalama and UdrakaRamputra
  • Enlightenment: At age of 35 under the Peepal tree at Urvula (Bodhgaya) on banks of river Niranjana (Falgu)
  • Mahaparinirvana (483 B.C.): At Kushinagar at age of 80
  • Symbols: Lotus and Bull - Birth, Horse - Renunciation, Bodhi Tree - Enlightenment, Dhammachakra Pravartana (Sarnath) - First sermon

questions.question: What was the pedestrian path for devotees to wave in homage to Stupa called in Buddhist architecture?
questions.solution:
Medhi
Features of Stupa:
  • Medhi - A circular terrace
  • Toranas - wall with decorated gateways
  • Anda - hemispherical mound
  • Chattra - A central pillar supporting a triple-umbrella form
  • Harmika - A square railing

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Lion Capital of Ashoka:
1. The Lion Capital was built to commemorate the death (Mahaparinirvana) of Buddha.
2. It was originally erected at Sarnath by Emperor Ashoka.
3. It was adopted as the National Emblem of India in 1950.
Which of the statements given above is incorrect?
questions.solution:
1 only
The Lion Capital was not built to mark Buddha's death; rather it commemorates the First Sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) delivered at Sarnath. Emperor Ashoka erected it at Sarnath, and it was later adopted as the National Emblem of India in 1950.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct?
I. Gautama Buddha belonged to a small gana known as the Sakya gana and was a Kshatriya.
II. Gautama Buddha passed away at Kusinara.
questions.solution:
Both I and II
Important places related to the life of Buddha:
  • Birth - Lumbini
  • Enlightenment - Bodh Gaya (Bihar)
  • First Sermon (Dharma-Chakra-Pravartana) - Sarnath
  • Death/Mahaparinirvana - Kushinagara (Pali: Kusinara), Uttar Pradesh

questions.question: The earliest Buddhist texts were written in:
questions.solution:
Pali
Pali canon, also called Tipitaka (Pali: Triple Basket), is the complete canon, first recorded in Pali, of the Theravada ("Way of the Elders") branch of Buddhism.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Gandhara School of Art:
1. Marble stone was mainly used in this art style.
2. It was patronized by the Kushanas.
3. It shows a strong influence of Greek art.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
2 and 3 only
Statement 1 is incorrect because Gandhara art used grey sandstone, not marble. It was developed under the Kushanas (esp. Kanishka) and shows a strong Greek (Hellenistic) influence, therefore also called Greco-Buddhist art.

questions.question:
Match the Mahajanapada with its capital:
Column A: Mahajanapada Column B: Capital
1. Vatsa a. Kaushambi
2. Magadha b. Rajagriha
3. Kuru c. Ujjayini
4. Avanti d. Indraprastha
questions.solution:
1-a, 2-b, 3-d, 4-c
  • Vatsa: Capital was Kaushambi (near modern Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh)
  • Magadha: Capital was Rajagriha (later shifted to Pataliputra)
  • Kuru: Capital was Indraprastha (near modern Delhi)
  • Avanti: Capital was Ujjayini (in present-day Madhya Pradesh)

questions.question: When did the second urbanisation in Ganga Valley take place?
questions.solution:
6th Century BCE
This era witnessed the development of kingdoms and Mahajanapadas like Magadha, Kosala, and Vatsa, alongside advancements in agriculture, trade, and administration. The First urbanisation in India took place during the Harappan civilization.

questions.question:
Consider the following dynasties of Magadha during the Mahajanapada period:
1. Haryanka Dynasty
2. Shishunaga Dynasty
3. Nanda Dynasty
4. Maurya Dynasty
Which of the following gives the correct chronological order?
questions.solution:
1→2→3→4
  • Haryanka dynasty (544-412 BCE) - first ruling dynasty of Magadha, founded by Bimbisara
  • Shishunaga dynasty (412-344 BCE)
  • Nanda dynasty (344-322 BCE)
  • Maurya dynasty (322 BCE onward) - started with Chandragupta Maurya, marking the foundation of the Mauryan Empire

questions.question: How many Mahajanapadas were there during the age of Buddha?
questions.solution:
16
The references of 16 Mahajanapadas are found in Anguttara Nikaya (Buddhist literature) and Bhagavati Sutra (Jain texts). The list includes: Anga (Champa), Magadh (Rajgriha/Girivraja, later Pataliputra), Kasi (Kasi), Vatsa (Kausambi), Kosala (Sravasti), Saurasena (Mathura), Panchala (Ahichchhatra), Kuru (Indraprastha), Matsya (Viratnagar), Chedi (Sothivati/Banda), Avanti (Ujjain/Mahishmati), Gandhara (Taxila, Purushapura), Kamboj (Rajapura), Asmaka (Paithan/Pratisthan), Vajji (Vaishali), Malla (Kusinara).

questions.question:
Match the following Mahajanapadas with their modern-day locations:
List I (Mahajanapada) List II (Modern Location)
A. Kosala 1. Malwa and Madhya Pradesh
B. Magadha 2. Rawalpindi (Pakistan)
C. Gandhara 3. Uttar Pradesh
D. Avanti 4. Gaya and Patna (Bihar)
questions.solution:
A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1
Modern day names of other Mahajanapadas:
  • Munger and Bhagalpur (Anga)
  • Gaya and Patna (Magadha)
  • Banaras (Kashi)
  • Prayagraj (Vatsa)
  • Malwa and Madhya Pradesh (Avanti)
  • Rawalpindi (Gandhara)
  • North Bihar (Vajji)
  • Jaipur (Matsya)
  • Meerut and Haryana (Kuru)
  • Western Uttar Pradesh (Shurasena and Panchala)
  • Bundelkhand region (Chedi)
  • Rajouri, Hajra and North-West Frontier Province (Kamboj)
  • Banks of Godavari (Asmaka or Assaka)
  • Deoria and Uttar Pradesh (Malla)

questions.question: Rulers of Mahajanapadas in ancient India collected taxes on crops at the rate of ______ of what was produced.
questions.solution:
1/6th
Rulers of mahajanapadas in ancient India collected a tax called 'Bhaga' from the farmers in their region.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta Maurya
The Maurya Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE with the guidance of his teacher and advisor Chanakya (Kautilya). He overthrew the Nanda dynasty of Magadha and established the first large-scale empire in India.
  • Capital: Pataliputra (modern Patna, Bihar)
  • Chandragupta defeated Seleucus Nicator (Alexander's general) in 305 BCE and signed a treaty, giving Seleucus 500 war elephants
  • His reign laid the foundation of a strong centralized administration described in Arthashastra (by Chanakya)
  • Later, he abdicated the throne, became a Jain monk, and died at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka)
  • His successors were Bindusara (son) and Ashoka the Great (grandson)

questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, who were referred to as Shaikhzadas or Hindustanis?
questions.option_1: Central Asian nobles of Turkic origin serving the Mughals
questions.option_2: Rajput converts elevated to noble ranks for loyalty
questions.option_3: Persian-trained officers recruited from Safavid Iran
questions.option_4: Indigenous Muslims who held administrative posts under Mughal rule
questions.solution:
Indigenous Muslims who held administrative posts under Mughal rule
In Mughal administration, the nobility was divided into different groups based on ethnicity and origin, such as Turanis (Central Asians), Iranis (Persians), Afghans, Rajputs, and Deccanis. The term Shaikhzadas or Hindustanis referred to Indian-born Muslims, often descendants of early Muslim settlers or local converts, who rose to prominence in the Mughal bureaucracy and military. Unlike the foreign-born nobles, these Hindustanis had deeper local connections and played an important role in balancing the power structure of the Mughal nobility.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler is credited with the establishment of the spy system in his empire?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta Maurya
Chandragupta Maurya (321-297 BCE) founded the Mauryan Empire with the guidance of Chanakya, defeating the last Nanda ruler at Pataliputra. After the Seleucid-Mauryan war, he gained territories west of the Indus in exchange for 500 war elephants and also married Seleucus's daughter. His empire expanded across most of India except Kalinga and the far south. Later, Chandragupta converted to Jainism and died by fasting at Shravanabelagola, having migrated there with Acharya Bhadrabahu. Greek ambassador Megasthenes visited his court and wrote Indica, describing Pataliputra and the division of Indian society into seven classes.

questions.question:
With reference to the city administration of Mauryan Empire, consider the following statements.
A) Megasthenes put light on the Mauryan city administration.
B) The city council was divided into six committees.
C) City administration was well planned.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
A, B, C
The Mauryan Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE, was the first major empire in India. It stretched from the Oxus Valley to the Kaveri Delta, covering most of the subcontinent, with its capital at Pataliputra, a city fortified with 64 gates and 570 towers. Megasthenes, a Greek historian, documented India in his work Indica.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Edicts of Ashoka:
1. Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war and Ashoka's remorse after it.
2. Pillar Edict II defines Dhamma as compassion, truthfulness, and purity of life.
3. The Rummidei inscription marks Ashoka's visit to the birthplace of Buddha at Lumbini.
4. The Kandahar Greek Edicts were written in Prakrit and Chinese.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1, 2 and 3 only
  • Rock Edict XIII: Mentions the Kalinga war and Ashoka's change of heart
  • Pillar Edict II: Defines Dhamma
  • Rummidei Inscription: Marks Ashoka's pilgrimage to Lumbini
  • Kandahar Greek Edicts were written in Greek and Prakrit, not Chinese

questions.question: The name 'Piyadassi' is associated with whom among the following Mauryan kings?
questions.solution:
Ashoka
"Piyadassi" is an honorific epithet that means "He who regards others with kindness", "Humane", or "He who glances amiably".

questions.question: Deimachus, who was a Greek ambassador, came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king,
questions.solution:
Bindusara
Bindusara also known as "Amitrochates" or "Amitragata" by the Greeks, was the son of Chandragupta Maurya. Bindusara patronized the Ajivikas and was taught by the Ajivika Brahmin Pingalavatsa.

questions.question:
Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka - Identify the incorrect statement:
A. Rock Edict XIII highlights the Kalinga War and Ashoka's remorse.
B. Rock Edict XII talks about Ashoka's duties as a ruler and his commitment to Dharma.
C. Rock Edict X focuses on the ruler's responsibilities and promotion of Dharma.
Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
B only
  • Statement B is incorrect: Rock Edict XII does not talk about ruler duties; it emphasizes tolerance and respect for all religions
  • Statement A is correct: Rock Edict XIII mentions the Kalinga War and Ashoka's remorse
  • Statement C is correct: Rock Edict X describes the duties of the ruler and commitment to Dharma

questions.question: Who among the following generally used to head the provincial administration under the Mauryas?
questions.solution:
Kumara
The 18 Tirthas were key officials in ancient administration, including roles like Mantrin (Chief Minister), Purohita (Priest), Senapati (Army Commander), Yuvaraja (Prince), Dauvarika (Chief of Palace Attendants), Antarvamsika (Chief of the King's Guards), Prasasta (Magistrate), Samahata (Collector General), Samidhata (Chief Treasurer), and Pradesta (Commissioner). Other roles included Nayak (Town Guard), Paur (City Official).

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the basic attributes of Ashoka's Dhamma?
questions.solution:
Celibacy
Ashoka's Dhamma, as outlined in his Edicts, emphasized the following basic attributes:
  • Ahimsa (Non-violence)
  • Secularism (Separation of religion and state)
  • Political unification (Unity and harmony among subjects)

questions.question: Who among the following envoys was sent by Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
Megasthenes
He was an ancient Greek historian, diplomat, and ethnographer who authored the famous work "Indica", providing valuable insights into the Mauryan Empire, including its administration, society, geography, and culture.

questions.question: Which of the following Ashokan rock edicts declares prohibition of animal sacrifice?
questions.solution:
Major Rock Edict - I
There are 14 Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka in three languages (Prakrit, Aramaic and Greek) and two scripts (Brahmi and Kharosthi).
  • Major Rock Edict II - mentions social welfare under Dhamma
  • Major Rock Edict III - declares that respect for parents and for all living things, including Brahmans and Sramanas, is a virtue
  • Major Rock Edict IV - consideration and non-violence to animals and courtesy to relations
  • Major Rock Edict XIII - mentions Ashoka's victory over Kalinga

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghmitra to spread Buddhism in Sri Lanka.
Reason (R): Ashoka was the third Mauryan king and a devoted follower of Dhamma who promoted Buddhism abroad.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution:
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Ashoka, as a devoted follower of Dhamma, actively propagated Buddhism. He sent Mahendra and Sanghmitra to Sri Lanka to spread the teachings, making the assertion correct. The reason correctly explains why Ashoka undertook this mission.

questions.question: Bhabru-Bairat rock edicts mainly depicting Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism are found in
questions.solution:
Rajasthan
Bhabru is the only inscription in the postuphoden script (bi-directional script from right to left and left to right in an alternate line).

questions.question: Who requested the Syrian king to send a Greek philosopher?
questions.solution:
Bindusara
Bindusara was the second Mauryan emperor, father of Ashoka, and son of Chandragupta (founder of Mauryan empire). Syrian King Antiochus sent his ambassador Deimachus to the court of Bindusara.

questions.question: Barabar Cave, famously known for depicting Ashoka's inscription, is situated at
questions.solution:
Gaya, Bihar
The Barabar Caves, located in the Makhdumpur region of Jehanabad district, Bihar, date back to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE) and were built by Emperor Ashoka for Ajivika ascetics. The caves include Karan Chaupar, Lomas Rishi, Sudama, and Visvakarma Cave.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers was defeated in the battle for Pataliputra by Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
Dhana Nanda
He was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, and his defeat marked the establishment of the Mauryan Empire in India.

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan rulers was the first, who tried to convey his messages to his subjects concerning the idea and practice of dharma through inscriptions?
questions.solution:
Ashoka
Ashoka was the third emperor of the Mauryan Dynasty. To propagate the policy of dharma, he used the medium of edicts. These edicts were to communicate between the King (Ashoka) and his subjects. Few inscriptions were addressed to the Buddhist Sangha.
